headline: OptScientist uses a symbolic model and language-model research loop to search for optimization laws
summary: The preprint introduces OptScientist, which pairs a learned symbolic optimization model with an LLM-based research loop to propose and compare objective and constraint laws from data. On OptFeynman, a synthetic benchmark generated from 99 known physics-derived optimization problems, the authors report exact preference-order recovery on 88 discrete and 78 continuous problems. They also report results on human risky choice and quarterly U.S. monetary policy. The policy evaluation uses 127 quarters split into 90 training, 23 validation and 14 out-of-time test observations; the model reports 78.6% exact policy-stance accuracy and 85.7% direction accuracy, with substantial uncertainty. These paper-reported results do not demonstrate causal mechanisms, broad transfer or independently reproduced scientific discovery.
